questions.question: Sami receives a patient who wants a perfect smile. He says: 'Ceramic veneers are the solution!' Mina asks him: 'What if she has dark teeth?' What is a dental veneer?
options: A thin ceramic shell bonded to the outer surface of the tooth
A full crown covering the entire tooth
A professional peroxide whitening
A composite applied directly to the tooth
questions.explanation: Sami explains: 'Veneers are ultra-thin aesthetic restorations that improve the shape and color of teeth.' Mina adds: 'But they have limits for severe discolorations.'

questions.question: Mina examines a patient with yellow teeth. She offers whitening. Sami asks: 'Does whitening really work?' What is the principle of teeth whitening?
options: Active oxygen breaks down organic pigments in the enamel
A resin layer covers the tooth surface
A laser removes superficial stains
Enamel grinding to remove pigments
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'Hydrogen peroxide or carbamide peroxide releases oxygen that breaks down pigments.' Sami: 'And how long does it last?'

questions.question: Sami, seeing a fracture on an incisor, says: 'It needs a crown!' Mina responds: 'What about a veneer?' What is the difference between a veneer and a crown?
options: A veneer covers the outer surface, a crown covers the entire tooth
A veneer is more resistant than a crown
A crown is more aesthetic than a veneer
A veneer is only made in the laboratory
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'The veneer is less invasive and preserves tooth structure. The crown is indicated when the tooth is too fractured.' Sami: 'I'll go with the veneer then.'

questions.question: Mina, choosing a shade for a veneer, says: 'We must respect the value scale.' Sami asks: 'What is the value scale?'
options: The brightness of colors, from light to dark
The price of different veneers
The size of the chosen veneer
The brand of material used
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'The value scale measures the brightness of teeth, from A1 (lightest) to D4 (darkest).' Sami: 'I'll use the Vita scale!'

questions.question: Sami, preparing a veneer, says: 'We can prepare without anesthesia.' Mina responds: 'Not always!' When should anesthesia be used for a veneer?
options: If the preparation reaches the dentin or pulp
Never, it's always painless
Always, it's a legal obligation
Only on posterior molars
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'Superficial preparation can be painless, but as soon as dentin is touched, anesthesia is necessary.' Sami: 'I'll anesthetize as a precaution.'

questions.question: Mina, talking about ceramic veneers, says: 'They are very aesthetic but fragile.' Sami asks: 'When to use them?'
options: On anterior teeth with controlled occlusion
On molars for better resistance
On all teeth without any restriction
Only on primary temporary teeth
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'Ceramic veneers are indicated for anterior teeth, where aesthetics are paramount.' Sami: 'I'll offer them to patients who want a perfect smile.'

questions.question: Sami, seeing a smile with an asymmetrical gingival line, says: 'It's still aesthetic.' Mina responds: 'Not at all!' What is the gingival line?
options: The gum contour defining the visible crown
The color of the patient's gums
The thickness of gingival tissues
The position of teeth in the arch
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'The gingival line must be harmonious for an aesthetic smile. Asymmetry may require periodontal or orthodontic treatment.' Sami: 'I never thought of that!'

questions.question: Mina, analyzing a smile, says: 'The proportions are good.' Sami asks: 'What proportions?' What is the golden proportion concept in dental aesthetics?
options: The 1:1.618 ratio between the widths of central and lateral incisors
The ratio between tooth size and face size
The proportion between tooth color and eye color
The balance between tooth height and width
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'Golden proportions create natural harmony. The width of central incisors should be 1.618 times that of lateral incisors.' Sami: 'I'll measure that!'

questions.question: Sami, seeing a patient with spaced teeth, says: 'We close the diastemas with composite.' Mina responds: 'What about veneers?' When to use veneers to close diastemas?
options: For wide spaces with discolored or malformed teeth
Always, it's the best solution
Never, composite is enough
Only on lower molars
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'Direct composite is ideal for small diastemas. Veneers are indicated for more complex cases.' Sami: 'I'll offer both options.'

questions.question: Mina, talking about the smile, says: 'The smile line is essential.' Sami asks: 'What is it?'
options: The curve of the incisal edge when smiling
The color of teeth when smiling
The size of the patient's smile
The general shape of the face
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'The smile line should be harmonious and follow the curve of the lower lip.' Sami: 'I'll observe this line in my patients.'

questions.question: Sami, seeing a patient with tetracycline stains, says: 'Whitening will fix everything.' Mina responds: 'Not so sure!' What is the limitation of whitening?
options: It fails on tetracycline stains and severe fluorosis
It whitens all teeth without exception
It makes teeth stronger and more resistant
It has no limits in its effectiveness
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'Tetracycline stains are intra-dentinal and do not respond well to whitening. Veneers may be more indicated.' Sami: 'I'll offer veneers then.'

questions.question: Mina, choosing a material for a veneer, says: 'I prefer ceramic.' Sami asks: 'Why not composite?'
options: Ceramic resists stains and wear better
Composite is more expensive than ceramic
Ceramic is faster to fabricate
Composite is forbidden in aesthetics
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'Ceramic resists stains and wear better than composite.' Sami: 'I'm convinced, I'll use ceramic.'

questions.question: Sami, preparing a veneer, says: 'We prepare 0.5 mm.' Mina responds: 'That's enough.' What is the recommended preparation thickness for a ceramic veneer?
options: Between 0.3 and 0.7 millimeters
Between 1 and 2 millimeters
Between 3 and 4 millimeters
No preparation is necessary
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'A preparation of 0.3 to 0.7 mm is recommended for ceramic veneers.' Sami: 'I'll respect this thickness.'

questions.question: Mina, placing a veneer, says: 'Adhesion is crucial.' Sami asks: 'Why?'
options: To ensure retention and prevent debonding
To improve the veneer's color
To speed up the placement time
To reduce the cost of treatment
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'Good adhesion guarantees the longevity of the veneer.' Sami: 'I'll follow the adhesion protocol carefully.'

questions.question: Sami, seeing a debonded veneer, says: 'It's the patient's fault!' Mina responds: 'Not necessarily.' What are the causes of veneer debonding?
options: Poor adhesion, contamination, or occlusal forces
Only the patient's fault
Only the laboratory's fault
Only poor material quality
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'Debonding is often multifactorial.' Sami: 'I'll check my adhesion protocol.'

questions.question: Mina, talking about the smile, says: 'Gingival exposure is important.' Sami asks: 'What is it?'
options: The amount of gum visible when smiling
The natural color of the gum
The thickness of gingival tissues
The general shape of the gums
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'An aesthetic smile generally shows less than 2 mm of gum.' Sami: 'I'll measure gingival exposure in my patients.'

questions.question: Sami, seeing a smile with a deviated midline, says: 'It's not serious.' Mina responds: 'It's very important!' Why is the midline important?
options: It must align with the center of the face for harmony
It has no aesthetic importance
It must be deviated to look natural
It only concerns molars
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'The midline of the incisors must align with the center of the face for a harmonious smile.' Sami: 'I'll always check the alignment.'

questions.question: Mina, analyzing a smile, says: 'The tooth axis is good.' Sami asks: 'Why is the axis important?'
options: The tooth axis should be parallel to the facial axis
The tooth axis is not important
The axis should be tilted for aesthetics
The axis only concerns molars
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'A tilted tooth axis can give an asymmetrical smile.' Sami: 'I'll analyze tooth axes in the future.'

questions.question: Sami, seeing a patient with worn teeth, says: 'It's age.' Mina responds: 'Not always.' What are the causes of tooth wear?
options: Bruxism, acidic diet, aggressive brushing
Only natural aging
Only nighttime bruxism
Only acidic diet
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'Tooth wear can have multiple causes.' Sami: 'I'll look for the cause before treating.'

questions.question: Mina, seeing a patient with fluorosis, says: 'We need veneers.' Sami asks: 'What is fluorosis?'
options: Hypomineralization of enamel due to excess fluoride
Bacterial infection of enamel
Fluoride deficiency during childhood
Trauma to the permanent tooth
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'Fluorosis appears as white or brown spots on the enamel.' Sami: 'I'll offer veneers to mask the stains.'

questions.question: Sami, talking about the smile, says: 'The smile arc is perfect.' Mina asks: 'What is it?'
options: The curve of the incisal edge when smiling
The color of teeth when smiling
The overall size of the smile
The general shape of the face
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'The smile arc should be harmonious for a natural smile.' Sami: 'I'll always check the smile arc.'

questions.question: Mina, placing a veneer, says: 'The veneer needs to be polished.' Sami asks: 'Why?'
options: To improve aesthetics and hygiene
To make the veneer more resistant
To increase whitening
To speed up placement
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'Good polishing improves aesthetics and hygiene.' Sami: 'I'll always polish veneers.'

questions.question: Sami, seeing a patient with a gummy smile, says: 'It's aesthetic.' Mina responds: 'Not always.' What is a gummy smile?
options: A smile that shows too much gum
A smile with dark gums
A smile with swollen gums
A smile with no visible teeth
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'A gummy smile may require periodontal or aesthetic treatment.' Sami: 'I'll suggest a correction.'

questions.question: Mina, seeing a patient with overlapping teeth, says: 'Orthodontic treatment is necessary before veneers.' Sami asks: 'Why?'
options: Veneers require optimal tooth alignment
Veneers align teeth directly
Orthodontics is faster than veneers
Veneers are more expensive than orthodontics
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'Orthodontics creates the space and alignment needed before placing veneers.' Sami: 'I'll do orthodontics first.'

questions.question: Sami and Mina discuss the future of dental aesthetics. Sami says: '3D printing will replace traditional veneers.' Mina responds: 'Not so fast!' What is the future of aesthetics?
options: Technology complements traditional techniques
3D printing will replace all veneers
Traditional veneers will completely disappear
Dental aesthetics is a fixed discipline
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'Technologies evolve, but the art of the smile remains a human art.' Sami: 'I agree, we keep our know-how!'

questions.question: Mina and Sami discuss the perfect smile. Mina says: 'Symmetry is the key.' Sami asks: 'And imperfections?' What does the perfect smile represent in dental aesthetics?
options: A balance between form, color, and facial harmony
Only perfectly white teeth
Only perfectly aligned teeth
Only white and aligned teeth
questions.explanation: Mina explains: 'The perfect smile is a balance between dental aesthetics and facial harmony.' Sami: 'I'll always seek overall harmony.'
